concurrent_geometry_set.derivation: Every reconstruct call fully consumes the scratch before returning: the write (ext.reconstruct*) and the read (ext.hgemm / amax) are enqueued back-to-back on the same stream inside one eager function invocation, and no reference to the view survives the call (output goes to a separate tensor via hgemm). Distinct modules (gate, up, down, q, k, v, o, in_proj, ba, fc, head) are separate custom-op invocations, serialized on the model's forward stream. Therefore every reachable concurrent set is a singleton {one geometry}.
concurrent_geometry_set.baseline_already_assumes_serialization: the unpatched dict shares ONE buffer per geometry across all layers of that geometry (130 gate/up modules share one 5120x17408 buffer) and across target and MTP-draft models; any concurrent forward on a second stream would already race the baseline. The arena extends the identical assumption across geometries, adding no new requirement.
concurrent_geometry_set.arena_size_rule: max over concurrent sums = max over singletons = largest single geometry: 2*K*min(N,32768) bytes
concurrent_geometry_set.per_geometry_offsets: every view starts at arena byte offset 0 (singleton concurrency means no packing); alignment is the allocation's base alignment - the CUDA caching allocator returns >=512 B aligned blocks, and torch's Tensor.view(dtype) requires only element-size (2 B) alignment at offset 0, trivially satisfied. Verified by the harness: all views offset 0, in-bounds, fp16-aligned.
concurrent_geometry_set.with_head_geometry: baseline 1110.0 -> arena 320.0 MiB; head requires >=128 sampled logit rows and does not trigger at max_num_seqs 1-8 with MTP-3 (confirmed: no fourth growth line in either arena serve)

cuda_graph_interaction.is_reconstruct_inside_decode_graphs: no, at every profile we ship. The dispatch is a runtime row-count test inside the custom op: reconstruct needs m >= VLLM_EXL3_PREFILL_RECONSTRUCT_M = 128. FULL_DECODE_ONLY capture rows are bounded by cudagraph_capture_sizes: [4] at the qualified profile, [32] at the perf-sweep profile; _graph_decode_capture_rows (exl3.py:1047-1087) can only produce rows <= max capture size. 32 < 128, so captured replays always take the exl3_gemm/b12x branch and the scratch is graph-free.
cuda_graph_interaction.docs41_claim_confirmed: decode goes through b12x/exl3_gemm; reconstruct is a prefill path above RECONSTRUCT_M=128 - verified from the dispatch conditions at exl3.py:986-993 and :1287-1294
cuda_graph_interaction.exotic_config_guard: an operator could set capture sizes >= 128 with VLLM_EXL3_GRAPH_DECODE=1, putting reconstruct inside a captured graph. The patch handles it: serving the arena during capture freezes it (never reallocated afterwards); a geometry that no longer fits gets a dedicated persistent per-geometry buffer - exactly the pre-arena behaviour, so the worst case is the status quo. Verified by test_arena_never_grows_during_capture_and_freezes_afterwards and the harness capture_freeze section.
cuda_graph_interaction.priming_note: VLLM_EXL3_GRAPH_DECODE=1 priming (_prime_exl3_gemm_rows, exl3.py:1090-1169) runs eagerly pre-capture and only for capturable row counts, all < 128 in our profiles; it cannot touch the reconstruct path
